sentences.en: Today, as Joe Biden prepares to take the oath of office and become the 46th President of the United States, some of his

sentences.en: supporters are filled with hope, some with concern, but all with relief.

sentences.en: It's Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 今天是周三，

sentences.en: January 20th.
There he is.

sentences.en: Hey, Michael.

sentences.en: How's it going?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: It's been a long year, huh?
sentences.zh: 这是漫长的一年，对吧？

sentences.en: As it ever.
sentences.zh: 一如既往。

sentences.en: Boy, oh boy.
sentences.zh: 天哪，天哪。

sentences.en: Well, Brian, I'm sure you remember the last time that we talked.
sentences.zh: 好吧，布莱恩，我相信你还记得我们上次谈话的情景。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And let me refresh our listeners' memory, because you surely remember it.
sentences.zh: 让我帮听众们回忆一下，因为你肯定记得。

sentences.en: It was right before Super Tuesday in the middle of the Democratic primary, and you were a deeply conflicted Democratic voter because you loved Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 那是在民主党初选期间的“超级星期二”之前，你当时是一位内心极其矛盾的民主党选民，因为你很喜欢乔·拜登。

sentences.en: You had a personal connection with him dating back to your college days when he spoke at an event that you organized.
sentences.zh: 你和他有着深厚的个人渊源，可以追溯到你的大学时代，当时他在你组织的一次活动上发表过演讲。

sentences.en: And what you told us when we spoke to you back then was that you feared Joe Biden was not necessarily the right candidate
sentences.zh: 那时你告诉我们，你担心乔·拜登未必是击败伯尼·桑德斯的合适人选，

sentences.en: to beat back Bernie Sanders, who was ascendant at that moment, and whose views you disagreed with.
sentences.zh: 当时伯尼·桑德斯势头正盛，而你并不认同他的观点。

sentences.en: And you frankly feared that Joe Biden was not necessarily the right candidate to beat back President Trump.
sentences.zh: 而且你坦率地担心，乔·拜登未必是击败特朗普总统的合适人选。

sentences.en: And I want to just remind you what you said back then.
sentences.zh: 我想提醒你当时说了什么。

sentences.en: You said, so I love Joe.
sentences.zh: 你说，我爱乔。

sentences.en: Joe's my guy.
sentences.zh: 乔是我的老伙计。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But he has not been a strong candidate.
sentences.zh: 但他并不是一个强有力的候选人。

sentences.en: I think he doesn't look good.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他看起来状态不好。

sentences.en: I think he's not sounding good.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他听起来状态也不好。

sentences.en: And Joe Biden, who is a great guy, is playing by a rule book that was written in 1980, maybe 1972.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登是个好人，但他遵循的是一套1980年，甚至可能是1972年制定的规则。

sentences.en: And that's really concerning to me, because Donald Trump's going to fillet him very quickly.
sentences.zh: 这让我非常担心，因为唐纳德·特朗普会很快把他生吞活剥。

sentences.en: So just to put this very bluntly, you were wrong on both fronts, because Biden did beat Bernie Sanders on Super Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 所以直白地说，你在两方面都错了，因为拜登在“超级星期二”击败了伯尼·桑德斯。

sentences.en: And afterwards, he beat President Trump by 7 million votes.
sentences.zh: 此后，他又以700万票的优势击败了特朗普总统。

sentences.en: So is there anything you want to say for yourself?
sentences.zh: 那么，你有什么想为自己辩解的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: This is what my daughter calls the Brian Keene effect.
sentences.zh: 这就是我女儿所说的“布莱恩·基恩效应”。

sentences.en: That in fact, the very next day, Biden just rolled over everybody else and won all those primaries.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就在第二天，拜登横扫了所有人，赢得了所有那些初选。

sentences.en: It was unbelievable, right?
sentences.zh: 简直不可思议，对吧？

sentences.en: It was Virginia, it was South Carolina, it was everything.
sentences.zh: 那是弗吉尼亚州，那是南卡罗来纳州，那是所有的一切。

sentences.en: And he was the de facto nominee, literally the next day.
sentences.zh: 就在第二天，他实际上就成了事实上的提名人。

sentences.en: And that's the Joe we were looking for.
sentences.zh: 而那正是我们所期待的乔。

sentences.en: And by the way, the next day, I voted for Joe.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，第二天我就投了乔一票。

sentences.en: And so ultimately, the Democrats picked the right candidate to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，民主党人选出了正确的人选来完成这件事。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What do you think was at the core of your wrongness?
sentences.zh: 你认为你判断失误的核心原因是什么？

sentences.en: Not to put that too weirdly.
sentences.zh: 不是要把这个问题说得太奇怪。

sentences.en: Well, my wrongness was actually more, not so much a wrongness, as a struggle that I think a lot of
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的失误其实更多不是一种错误，而是一种挣扎，我想很多

sentences.en: voters were having, which is, do we go with kind of the dignity of a guy like Joe Biden, or the fight of either a Bernie Sanders or a Michael Bloomberg.
sentences.zh: 选民都有这种挣扎，那就是：我们是选择像乔·拜登这样的人的尊严，还是选择像伯尼·桑德斯或迈克尔·布隆伯格那样的斗志？

sentences.en: And that was really kind of the challenge.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一种挑战。

sentences.en: Which one is going to win?
sentences.zh: 哪一个会赢？

sentences.en: And actually, I think at the end of the day, what we saw, and I think what this
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为归根结底，我们所看到的，以及我认为这个

sentences.zh: 国家所看到的，尤其是现在，确实是像拜登这样的人的尊严赢得了人心。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: In our original conversation, what you seemed to fear was that Biden, in terms of his energy,
sentences.zh: 在我们最初的谈话中，你似乎担心拜登在精力、

sentences.en: his presence, his very nature, might not be up for the task of winning the primary and beating
sentences.zh: 风度以及他的本性方面，可能无法胜任赢得初选和击败

sentences.en: Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的任务。

sentences.en: And if that was your fear back then, is it your fear that he might not be up to the challenge of this very unique and pretty dark moment, now that he has won, which is somehow
sentences.zh: 如果那是你当时的担忧，那么现在他已经赢了，你是否担心他可能无法应对这个非常独特且相当黑暗的时刻的挑战，也就是

sentences.zh: 是的，问得好。

sentences.en: That's a, it's a good point from before to now.
sentences.zh: 这是一个从过去到现在都很好的切入点。

sentences.zh: 对我来说，他在竞选过程中的表现证明了他的能力。

sentences.en: And in part, well, because he's been so consistent in not taking the bait.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，他始终如一地没有上钩。

sentences.en: And he was always kind of above it.
sentences.zh: 他总是表现得超然物外。

sentences.en: And it was like, oh, this is a guy, he's not going to get down there and play that name-calling game.
sentences.zh: 就像是，哦，这是一个不会去参与那种互相谩骂游戏的人。

sentences.en: He's going to keep focused and do the job.
sentences.zh: 他会保持专注，做好工作。

sentences.en: And you can see it already happening.
sentences.zh: 你已经可以看到这种情况正在发生。

sentences.en: Dignity, what you would call dignity.
sentences.zh: 尊严，你所说的尊严。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: And it was like, oh, he's already president.
sentences.zh: 就像是，哦，他已经是总统了。

sentences.en: It sounds like you're saying that Joe Biden will model the unity he wants himself in his conduct as president.
sentences.zh: 听起来你是说乔·拜登会以身作则，通过他作为总统的行为来塑造他所追求的团结。

sentences.en: And so I wonder what signs or images or rhetoric you will see from him that makes you think that he's on the right track towards trying to build unity in this moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，你会从他身上看到什么样的迹象、形象或言辞，让你认为他在这个时刻正走在建立团结的正确轨道上？

sentences.en: Well, in order to build unity, I think we have to kind of almost break some of the, the notions that we assume, which is what is unity?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了建立团结，我认为我们必须打破一些我们默认的观念，那就是：什么是团结？

sentences.en: Because quite frankly, to some folks, unity sounds like weakness right now.
sentences.zh: 因为坦率地说，对某些人来说，团结现在听起来像是软弱。

sentences.en: Oh, you know what?
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道吗？

sentences.en: We're not going to have unity.
sentences.zh: 我们不会有团结。

sentences.en: How can I stand there with, you know, people who are, who have quite frankly, stood and watched people invade the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我怎么能和那些，你知道，坦率地说，站在那里看着人们入侵美国

sentences.en: Capitol?
sentences.zh: 国会大厦的人站在一起呢？

sentences.en: Like they have to be punished firSt. Like we can't just be unified with these people.
sentences.zh: 他们必须先受到惩罚。我们不能就这样和这些人团结起来。

sentences.en: This is, there has to be a punishment first before we can just be unified.
sentences.zh: 这，必须先有惩罚，我们才能谈团结。

sentences.en: People need to be held accountable before you can say everything's okay.
sentences.zh: 在你说一切都好之前，人们需要被追究责任。

sentences.en: And that, I think that's true whether someone's five years old and they broke a window and you can't just say, hey, no, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是事实，无论是一个五岁的孩子打破了窗户，你不能只是说，嘿，没关系。

sentences.en: You have to actually show that, no, you actually have to, you know, fix the problem before you can say, hey, you're never going to do it again.
sentences.zh: 你必须实际表现出，不，你实际上必须，你知道，在说“你永远不会再这样做了”之前，先解决问题。

sentences.en: And a coup attempt on the United States of America from within, I mean, that was, it is unbelievably scary.
sentences.zh: 而一场从内部发起的针对美利坚合众国的政变企图，我的意思是，那真是，令人难以置信地可怕。

sentences.en: It's scarier to me than 9-11.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，它比9·11事件更可怕。

sentences.en: I mean, that day I was talking to my children and I'm like, do you understand these are not, this is not a foreign invader.
sentences.zh: 那天我在和我的孩子们谈话，我说，你们明白吗，这些人不是，这不是外国侵略者。

sentences.en: These are our neighbors.
sentences.zh: 这些人是我们的邻居。

sentences.en: These are people from just, you know, an hour flight away.
sentences.zh: 这些人来自，你知道，一小时航程之外的地方。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like, this is, we've never ever seen anything like this and that needs to be fixed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像是，我们从未见过这样的事情，这需要被修正。

sentences.en: So it never happens again.
sentences.zh: 这样它就永远不会再发生了。

sentences.en: But there's real opportunity here to, by the way, use that as an opportunity to bring together the country and say, yeah, you know what?
sentences.zh: 但这里确实有真正的机会，顺便说一句，利用这个机会把国家团结起来，说，是的，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I am Joe Biden and I am the president and this is how this is going to be fixed.
sentences.zh: 我是乔·拜登，我是总统，这就是解决这个问题的方法。

sentences.en: And there's your strength.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的力量所在。

sentences.en: Well, what if dignity and modeling unity and reaching across the aisle just isn't enough
sentences.zh: 那么，如果尊严、塑造团结和跨党派合作还不够，

sentences.en: and just does not convince, and there's very good reason to think it might not convince tens of
sentences.zh: 而且无法说服——并且有充分的理由认为它可能无法说服数千万被告知拜登的胜利是非法的共和党人——让他们视他为总统，从而实现任何愈合呢？

sentences.en: millions of Republicans who have been told Biden's victory is illegitimate to see him as their president and for there to be any healing?
sentences.zh: 这是你担心的吗？

sentences.en: Is that something you fear?
sentences.zh: 嗯，总的来说，人们的本性是善良的。

sentences.en: Well, by and large, people are of good nature.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们真的需要记住这一点，我们确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think we really need to remember that, that we really are.
sentences.zh: 现在，当我们被唤起最坏的本性时，我们所有人都容易表现出最坏的一面，包括我自己。

sentences.en: Now, when we're called to our worst natures, all of us are prone to actually perk up to our worst nature and myself included.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只需要，如果我们能被唤起最好的本性，我们其实已经做到了。

sentences.en: So we just, if we can be called to our best nature, we really, we're there already.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一点。

sentences.en: So that's kind of number one.
sentences.zh: 我真正认为引人注目的是社交媒体，尤其是推特，坦率地说，这对言论自由是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: And what I really could think is fascinating is just social media, Twitter particularly, is a real challenge for free speech, quite frankly.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到，一旦特朗普不再使用推特，假新闻就急剧下降了。

sentences.en: And we've seen as soon as Trump is now off Twitter, the fake news is, you know, is dropping precipitously.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说简直不可思议，事实上，美国总统竟然是制造这些假新闻的人。

sentences.en: And that is unbelievable to me that in fact, the president of the United
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是，好吧，你知道，我不能在拥挤的电影院里喊着火了。

sentences.en: States has been the one to create this fake news.
sentences.zh: 也许我不应该有权对一百万人撒谎。

sentences.en: And so it's kind of like, okay, well, you know, I can't call fire in a crowded movie theater.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上可能有助于共和国的生存。

sentences.en: Maybe I shouldn't be able to say a lie to a million people.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，关掉那个水龙头就是迈向团结的一步。

sentences.en: And that then actually may help the republic survive.
sentences.zh: 巨大的。

sentences.en: So you're saying just, just turning off that faucet is a step toward unity.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实是巨大的。

sentences.en: Huge.
sentences.zh: 现在问题还没有解决。

sentences.en: I mean, it really is huge.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，但这确实是一个巨大的进步，就像是，哦，大家等一下。

sentences.en: Now the problem's not fixed.
sentences.zh: 我们其实并没有那么讨厌彼此，因为我刚刚发现你并没有我想象中那么糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, but it is a huge step and it's, it's like, Oh, hang on everybody.
sentences.zh: 我只是不断地被灌输关于你有多糟糕的信息。

sentences.en: We really don't hate each other that much because I just found out that you're not as terrible a person as I had thought.
sentences.zh: 如果我不被灌输那些关于你有多糟糕的持续信息，因为你其实并没有那么糟糕，那么也许我们真的可以进行一次真正的对话。

sentences.en: I just, I'm being fed constant information about how terrible you are.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我们必须相处融洽、手拉手，但也许你并不是那么糟糕的人。

sentences.en: And if I am not fed that constant information about how terrible you are, because you're not really that terrible, then maybe we can actually have a real conversation.
sentences.zh: 就像我们不必谈论，哦天哪，你知道，你能相信他做了什么吗？

sentences.en: Not that we all have to get along and hold hands, but maybe you're just not that terrible a person.
sentences.zh: 还有，哦，我喜欢他做的事。

sentences.en: Like we don't have to talk about, Oh my God, you know, can you believe what he did?
sentences.zh: 哦，他讨厌这些人。

sentences.en: Oh, he hates these people.

sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，布莱恩·基恩的理论是：切断错误信息的流动，就职一位代表尊严、让美国政治整体降温的总统，减少全天的戏剧性事件。

sentences.en: Like, it's like, no, we don't have to do that.

sentences.en: So just to summarize that the

sentences.en: Brian Keene theory of the case here is turn off the flow of misinformation, inaugurate a president

sentences.en: who represents dignity and a generally lower temperature in American politics, creates less drama all day.

sentences.zh: 你和他一起经历了一段漫长的政治旅程，从怀疑到喜爱，但你第一次见到他时就有那个梦想。

sentences.en: By putting Biden in place, we are restoring the first brick of dignity to the United States and to the world.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他做到了，他也赢了，你害怕吗？

sentences.en: I remember you telling me that when you were a young man in college and you first met Joe Biden,
sentences.zh: 你感到感激吗？

sentences.en: you came to speak at your political union, you had dreamed he would run for president.
sentences.zh: 你感到紧张吗？

sentences.en: You'd go on a long political journey with him of skepticism and then affection, but you had that dream when you first met him.
sentences.zh: 你感到兴奋吗？

sentences.en: So now that he has done it and he has won, are you scared?
sentences.zh: 考虑到他从周三中午开始将面临的挑战，你现在的心情如何？

sentences.en: Are you grateful?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是，好吧。

sentences.en: Are you nervous?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是，好吧。

sentences.en: Are you excited?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是，好吧。

sentences.en: And where is your mood knowing the challenges that he's going to face starting at noon on Wednesday?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是，好吧。

sentences.en: Well, that's so, all right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是，好吧。

sentences.en: So I was, I met him in 89, 1989, and it's now 2021.
sentences.zh: 我是在89年，1989年遇见他的，现在已经是2021年了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So this is working out just like we planned, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这一切正按我们计划的那样进行，对吧？

sentences.en: 40 years later.
sentences.zh: 40年过去了。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: 31, 30 some odd years later now, right?
sentences.zh: 31年，30多年过去了，对吧？

sentences.en: This is exactly like we planned.
sentences.zh: 这完全符合我们的计划。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is unbelievably to me, this is the moment meeting the man.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这简直不可思议，这就是见到那个人的时刻。

sentences.en: I swear to God.
sentences.zh: 我发誓。

sentences.en: And he ran in 88, he ran in 2007.
sentences.zh: 他参加了88年的竞选，也参加了2007年的竞选。

sentences.en: This is the moment meeting the man.
sentences.zh: 这就是见到那个人的时刻。

sentences.en: And I swear, if he had won the other times, it would not be this momentous.
sentences.zh: 我发誓，如果他之前赢了，就不会有现在这么重大的意义。

sentences.en: But today, this is a president that this country needs
sentences.zh: 但今天，这就是这个国家所需要的总统，

sentences.en: right now after Trump.
sentences.zh: 就在特朗普之后。

sentences.en: You know, we always say politics is a pendulum.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们常说政治就像钟摆。

sentences.en: This is that swinging pendulum, but it is not the pendulum of left and right.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个摆动的钟摆，但它不是左右之争的钟摆。

sentences.en: It's the pendulum of personality.
sentences.zh: 它是人格的钟摆。

sentences.en: And this is the personality that we need, a man who's going to restore dignity through his own actions, his own
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们需要的人格，一个通过自己的行动、自己的

sentences.en: faith and his own faith in the American people to actually restore dignity to our country.
sentences.zh: 信念以及对美国人民的信念，真正恢复我们国家尊严的人。

sentences.en: And actually, quite frankly, to each other.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，也是为了彼此恢复尊严。

sentences.en: We're going to be better people to each other.
sentences.zh: 我们会对彼此更好。

sentences.en: And we need to be because we are.
sentences.zh: 我们需要这样做，因为我们本该如此。

sentences.en: Well, Brian, I want to thank you for making time for us again.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩，我想感谢你再次抽出时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Anytime.
sentences.zh: 随时都可以。

sentences.en: I really thank you for doing, kind of having these discussions.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感谢你进行这些讨论。

sentences.en: I think it's really important, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我认为这非常重要。

sentences.en: And I really think, I know there's a lot of concern and angst across the country about just about all of this.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为，我知道全国上下对这一切都充满了担忧和焦虑。

sentences.en: But I think we're a step closer to really unbelievable days ahead for all of us.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们离我们所有人那令人难以置信的未来又近了一步。

sentences.en: I wonder, there are so many people who would expect you to feel this deep sense of relief and excitement.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，有很多人会期待你感到一种深深的宽慰和兴奋。

sentences.en: And I'm curious how close, how accurate that is, how close that comes to your feelings now.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道这有多准确，和你现在的感受有多接近。

sentences.en: Oh, you know, I'm Jenny Medina, a politics reporter with The Times.
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道，我是珍妮·梅迪纳，《时报》的政治记者。

sentences.en: I met Erica Andiola earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年早些时候见过埃里卡·安迪奥拉。

sentences.en: She's an immigration policy activist in Arizona who famously heckled Biden over the Obama administration's immigration record during a debate in the primaries.
sentences.zh: 她是亚利桑那州的一名移民政策活动家，曾在初选辩论中因奥巴马政府的移民记录而公开质问拜登。

sentences.en: I'm running because so many people.
sentences.zh: 我参选是因为有太多人。

sentences.en: And yet.
sentences.zh: 然而。

sentences.en: The day that Biden won the election, I know he has been winning it so many times, but the day that we
sentences.zh: 拜登赢得选举的那天，我知道他已经赢过很多次了，但那天我们

sentences.en: knew that Biden was going to be the president, I did.
sentences.zh: 知道拜登将成为总统时，我确实感受到了。

sentences.en: I felt, I literally physically felt a sense of relief that we didn't have to keep on figuring out what was going to be the next attack coming from the administration.
sentences.zh: 我感到，我真真切切地从身体上感受到了一种宽慰，因为我们不必再时刻提防政府接下来会发动什么攻击。

sentences.en: And that felt really great in my body and my mind.
sentences.zh: 这让我的身心都感到非常棒。

sentences.en: The next day, you know, it was just kind of getting up to like, okay, what's the next, what's the next move?
sentences.zh: 第二天，你知道，就像是起床后想，好吧，下一步是什么？

sentences.en: What's the next fight?
sentences.zh: 下一场战斗是什么？

sentences.en: And understanding that for immigrants, for people who tend to be the targets for Republicans, right?
sentences.zh: 并且明白对于移民，对于那些容易成为共和党目标的人来说，对吧？

sentences.en: If you hear political ads on TV from a Democrat and a Republican, a Republican is going to be campaigning around immigration.
sentences.zh: 如果你在电视上听到民主党人和共和党的政治广告，共和党人肯定会围绕移民问题进行竞选。

sentences.en: A Democrat is not going to say anything most of the time about immigration.
sentences.zh: 而民主党人大多数时候对移民问题只字不提。

sentences.en: And so we're not a priority for the most part.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在很大程度上不是优先事项。

sentences.en: And so I think for me, it's not just relief.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对我来说，这不仅仅是宽慰。

sentences.en: I think it's just now I feel a sense of urgency to start pressuring, you know, Biden again and start the accountability to make sure that immigration is a priority for him and his
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在我有一种紧迫感，要开始再次向拜登施压，开始问责，确保移民问题成为他和他的

sentences.en: administration.
sentences.zh: 政府的优先事项。

sentences.en: What's your, what's your biggest fear?
sentences.zh: 你最大的恐惧是什么？

sentences.en: What are you worried about under the Biden administration?
sentences.zh: 你担心拜登政府的什么？

sentences.en: Is it just being ignored or is it more than that?
sentences.zh: 是担心被忽视，还是不仅仅如此？

sentences.en: My biggest fear?
sentences.zh: 我最大的恐惧？

sentences.en: Well, there's a lot, but I think one of them is that
sentences.zh: 嗯，有很多，但我认为其中之一是

sentences.en: a lot of progressives and Democrats have this, this understanding that under the governance of a
sentences.zh: 许多进步派和民主党人有一种理解，认为在

sentences.en: Democrat, immigrants are okay.
sentences.zh: 民主党执政下，移民就没事了。

sentences.en: The same people who are rallying against kids in cages are now many thinking that everything's going to be fine.
sentences.zh: 那些曾经抗议“笼中儿童”的人，现在有许多人认为一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: And I just hope that we can create enough public awareness that people understand that we still have to push and that I really think that we're going
sentences.zh: 我只是希望我们能唤起足够的公众意识，让人们明白我们仍然必须推动变革，我真的认为我们

sentences.en: to have a lot more progress and that things are not going to be like under the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 会取得更多进展，事情不会像特朗普政府时期那样。

sentences.en: But also that things are not going to be perfect, that we're still going to have detention centers and people who are driving down the street and getting pulled over for a speeding
sentences.zh: 但也明白事情不会完美，我们仍然会有拘留中心，仍然会有开车时因为超速

sentences.en: ticket and getting deported.
sentences.zh: 罚单而被拦下并被驱逐出境的人。

sentences.en: And the only way that that's going to stop is if we as progressives or people who care about immigrants are willing to also hold accountable a Democratic president.
sentences.zh: 而阻止这一切的唯一方法，就是我们作为进步派或关心移民的人，也愿意去问责一位民主党总统。

sentences.en: I really hope that the public is there and those folks who were rallying against kids in cages that that they're continuing to rally with us.
sentences.zh: 我真的希望公众能站出来，那些曾经抗议“笼中儿童”的人能继续与我们并肩作战。

sentences.en: We'll see how things evolve.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待事态的发展。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 你在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间去探索付费墙后的内容，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请下载

sentences.en: Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 《时报》应用，今天就获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: My name is Kristen Urquiza.
sentences.zh: 我叫克里斯汀·乌尔基萨。

sentences.en: I'm 39 years old.
sentences.zh: 我今年39岁。

sentences.en: I jumped for joy when I heard of Kamala as the VP pick and it made me so excited for the entire ticket.
sentences.zh: 当我听说卡玛拉被选为副总统候选人时，我高兴得跳了起来，这让我对整个竞选组合感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: For me, seeing Vice President-elect Harris as the person
sentences.zh: 对我来说，看到当选副总统哈里斯作为

sentences.en: who an old white man, no offense to Joe Biden, is turning to as his right-hand person, that to me shatters
sentences.zh: 一位老白人男性（对乔·拜登没有冒犯之意）转而寻求的得力助手，这对我来说打破了

sentences.en: nearly as many glass and concrete ceilings as having somebody in that ultimate position.
sentences.zh: 几乎和让某人担任最高职位一样多的玻璃和混凝土天花板。

sentences.en: I kept saying, listen to this, Madam Vice President-elect.
sentences.zh: 我一直在说，听听这个，当选副总统女士。

sentences.en: I said it to anybody who would listen, my husband, my kids.
sentences.zh: 我对任何愿意听的人都说了，我的丈夫，我的孩子们。

sentences.en: I said, listen, Madam Vice President-elect, doesn't that have a great ring to it?
sentences.zh: 我说，听着，当选副总统女士，这听起来是不是很棒？

sentences.en: So often we as Black women are forced to wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 我们黑人女性常常被迫戴上面具。

sentences.en: The mask that we wear in public is a mask that may not allow you to see who we really are.
sentences.zh: 我们在公共场合戴的面具，可能让人无法看到我们真实的模样。

sentences.en: And I think that we are muffled in many instances because of preconceived notions about Black women.
sentences.zh: 我认为由于对黑人女性的先入之见，我们在许多情况下被压制了。

sentences.en: And to see her in that office, I want her to be able to maybe allow more Black women to feel confident and being able to take off that mask other places than just at home.
sentences.zh: 看到她坐在那个办公室里，我希望她能让更多的黑人女性感到自信，能够摘下那个面具，不仅仅是在家里。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm okay.
sentences.zh: 我还好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: I'm hanging in, you know.
sentences.zh: 我还在坚持，你知道的。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: This is Nina Patuk.
sentences.zh: 这是尼娜·帕图克。

sentences.en: We first spoke to Sharonda Bossier back in the summer.
sentences.zh: 我们第一次采访莎隆达·博西尔是在夏天。

sentences.en: She's a 36-year-old activist who had been organizing as a part of the Black Lives Matter movement for years.
sentences.zh: 她是一位36岁的活动家，多年来一直是“黑人的命也是命”运动的组织者。

sentences.en: When we spoke, the movement was newly energized by the ongoing protests and the outpouring of support following the police killing of George Floyd.
sentences.zh: 我们交谈时，这场运动因乔治·弗洛伊德被警察杀害后持续的抗议和如潮水般的支持而焕发了新的活力。

sentences.en: Then, the national conversation shifted to the election and the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 随后，全国的讨论转向了选举和大流行。

sentences.en: We wanted to see if the Biden administration felt like a new opportunity for the movement.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看拜登政府是否让这场运动感觉到了新的机遇。

sentences.en: You know, I think what's interesting is that many of the activists I have gotten to know
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为有趣的是，我所认识并相处过的许多活动家

sentences.en: and spend time with definitely were hoping for a more progressive candidate to end up at the top of the Democratic ticket.
sentences.zh: 绝对都希望有一位更进步的候选人最终成为民主党的领跑者。

sentences.en: And we ended up with Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 但我们最终得到的是乔·拜登。

sentences.en: And so, Biden, for many of us, is a compromise.
sentences.zh: 所以，对我们许多人来说，拜登是一种妥协。

sentences.en: He is a moderate by all accounts and all measures, right?
sentences.zh: 从各方面和各标准来看，他都是一个温和派，对吧？

sentences.en: But we definitely understood that it was critically important that he be elected to reducing the harm experienced by so many of us,
sentences.zh: 但我们绝对明白，选举他对于减少我们许多人、

sentences.en: our families, and other members of our community.
sentences.zh: 我们的家庭以及我们社区其他成员所遭受的伤害至关重要。

sentences.en: Sharonda and many of her fellow activists also have complicated feelings about Kamala Harris, namely because of her experience in law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 莎隆达和她的许多活动家同伴对卡玛拉·哈里斯也有复杂的感情，主要是因为她在执法部门的经历。

sentences.en: A friend of mine made me a customized pair of Tim's that say Kamala across the back.
sentences.zh: 我的一个朋友为我定制了一双Timberland靴子，后跟写着Kamala。

sentences.en: I don't know where if I will ever wear them, but I own them, right?
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否会穿它们，但我拥有它们，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they represent this moment and they represent what she represents to so many of us, complicated or not.
sentences.zh: 因为它们代表了这个时刻，也代表了她对我们许多人所象征的意义，无论复杂与否。

sentences.en: But they also see the potential for greater opportunity with Harris than with Biden.
sentences.zh: 但他们也看到了哈里斯比拜登带来更大机遇的潜力。

sentences.en: I would much rather organize to push and sway and educate her.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿去组织、推动、影响和教育她。

sentences.en: I think there's real hope that she will move.
sentences.zh: 我认为她会做出改变，这有着真正的希望。

sentences.en: I think she has demonstrated an openness to learning.
sentences.zh: 我认为她表现出了学习的开放态度。

sentences.en: And I also think that she, like many people of color, right, who have worked in law enforcement, are trying in this particular
sentences.zh: 我也认为她，像许多有色人种一样，对吧，那些曾在执法部门工作过的人，正在这个特定的

sentences.en: moment to reconcile with and for themselves what that means.
sentences.zh: 时刻试图与自己和解，去理解这意味着什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What do you want the administration's first hundred days to look like?
sentences.zh: 你希望政府的前一百天是什么样子？

sentences.en: Whew.
sentences.zh: 呼。

sentences.en: Listen.
sentences.zh: 听着。

sentences.en: I have so many thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我有很多想法。

sentences.en: I will be fully transparent and I will say that I don't think that Biden gave us much to vote for.
sentences.zh: 我会完全透明地说，我不认为拜登给了我们多少值得投票的理由。

sentences.en: I think Trump gave us a lot to vote againSt. I don't think
sentences.zh: 我认为特朗普给了我们很多反对他的理由。我不认为

sentences.en: I'm saying anything new or original here, right, when I say that we have watched Donald Trump provide legitimacy and political cover for violent extremists.
sentences.zh: 我在说些什么新奇或原创的东西，对吧，当我们说我们目睹了唐纳德·特朗普为暴力极端分子提供合法性和政治掩护时。

sentences.en: So often, you know, the media will talk about, well, there was a BLM protest and a counter proteSt. And you're like, that's not a, that's not, it's not the same.
sentences.zh: 通常，你知道，媒体会谈论，嗯，有一场BLM抗议和一场反抗议。你会觉得，那不是，那不是，那不是一回事。

sentences.en: And I think because so much of the public conversation has been framed as two sides with two different worldviews.
sentences.zh: 我认为因为太多的公共讨论被框定为两种有着不同世界观的对立面。

sentences.en: The ideas of the far and fringe right have been made legitimate because there is this sense that you can enact racial violence and that the state has your back.
sentences.zh: 极右翼的思想变得合法化了，因为有一种感觉，认为你可以实施种族暴力，而国家会支持你。

sentences.en: And we have seen it, I think, you know, especially in the last four years, it's just, it's created for me anyway.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了，我想，你知道，特别是在过去四年里，这对我来说，它只是创造了。

sentences.en: There's just overwhelming sense that people feel empowered to harm me and don't feel like there will be any real consequences if they do.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种压倒性的感觉，觉得他们有权伤害我，并且不觉得如果他们这样做会有任何真正的后果。

sentences.en: This belief is why Sharonda worries about the safety of the incoming administration.
sentences.zh: 这种信念就是莎隆达担心新政府安全的原因。

sentences.en: It's a worry that's been with her essentially since the moment Biden was elected.
sentences.zh: 这种担忧基本上从拜登当选的那一刻起就一直伴随着她。

sentences.en: I felt relief and tried very hard to sit with that for a moment.
sentences.zh: 我感到宽慰，并努力让自己在那一刻平静下来。

sentences.en: And then I felt almost an immediate sense of, of dread chiefly because I was worried about what the backlash would look like from the right.
sentences.zh: 然后我几乎立刻感到一种恐惧，主要是因为我担心来自右翼的反弹会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And I was worried about the increased scrutiny to which Kamala would be subjected.
sentences.zh: 我也担心卡玛拉会受到更严格的审查。

sentences.en: And I think it's probably a feeling that was most akin to the feeling I experienced when Obama was elected in 08.
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是一种感觉，最类似于我在08年奥巴马当选时所经历的感觉。

sentences.en: This like, man, we just made history.
sentences.zh: 就像是，天哪，我们刚刚创造了历史。

sentences.en: And also I'm so afraid for this person.
sentences.zh: 同时我也为这个人感到非常害怕。

sentences.en: And I feel that for Kamala every time I see her.
sentences.zh: 每次看到卡玛拉，我都有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Can you talk a little bit about where that fear comes from?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这种恐惧从何而来吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the fear that I'm describing, right, this fear of, you know, you're a history maker, you're a trailblazer, what are they going to do to you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我所描述的这种恐惧，对吧，这种恐惧，你知道，你是历史的创造者，你是开拓者，他们会对你做什么？

sentences.en: You know, really comes from the history of
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的源于这个国家

sentences.en: Black people in this country, right?
sentences.zh: 黑人的历史，对吧？

sentences.en: Every time we have broken a barrier, every time we have tried to stand up for our humanity, every time we have tried to fully participate in this society, there are
sentences.zh: 每一次我们打破障碍，每一次我们试图为我们的人性挺身而出，每一次我们试图充分参与这个社会，都有

sentences.en: examples of very real and violent pushback from people who have believed that we should stay in our place, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 来自那些认为我们应该“安分守己”的人的非常真实和暴力的反击例子。

sentences.en: And I think even if you listen to, you know, the ways that we talk about, particularly women who are trailblazers, I think all of the messages we get around that are,
sentences.zh: 我想即使你听听，你知道，我们谈论的方式，特别是关于那些开拓者的女性，我认为我们围绕这一点得到的所有信息都是，

sentences.en: if you dare try and be the first of anything, right, we are going to pick you apart.
sentences.zh: 如果你敢尝试成为任何事情的第一人，对吧，我们就会把你撕成碎片。

sentences.en: And I think that's especially true for Black women and women of color.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对黑人女性和有色人种女性来说尤其如此。

sentences.en: What are you most worried about as you look ahead to the Biden administration?
sentences.zh: 当你展望拜登政府时，你最担心的是什么？

sentences.en: I am really, really nervous that we are going to attempt to appease the people who rioted at the
sentences.zh: 我真的，真的非常紧张，我们将会试图安抚那些在……暴乱的人。

sentences.en: Capitol.
sentences.zh: 国会大厦。

sentences.en: And that those of us who have experienced real harm and real violence, specifically over the
sentences.zh: 而那些像我们这样经历过真正伤害和暴力的人，特别是在

sentences.en: past four years, will be asked in the name of reconciliation, to not bring up that harm, right, and to not hold accountable the people who committed that harm against us.
sentences.zh: 过去四年里，会被要求以和解的名义，不要再提起那些伤害，对吧，也不要追究那些对我们造成伤害的人的责任。

sentences.en: And you've already spoken about some of your hopes for the administration, but I'm wondering, what are your hopes for yourself?
sentences.zh: 你已经谈到了一些你对本届政府的期望，但我很好奇，你对自己有什么期望？

sentences.en: Honestly, I'm hopeful that I find myself less angry on a regular and consistent basis.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我希望自己能少一些经常性和持续性的愤怒。

sentences.en: I have over the past four years, really, really just harbored this deep sense of anger and resentment
sentences.zh: 在过去的四年里，我真的，真的只是怀着一种深深的愤怒和怨恨，

sentences.en: at this country, at the people who voted for him, at the people who legitimized him.
sentences.zh: 对这个国家，对那些投票给他的人，对那些使他合法化的人。

sentences.en: And it has gotten to the point where I listen to the news in the morning, and I'm like shouting back at my phone.
sentences.zh: 以至于现在我早上听新闻时，都会对着手机大喊大叫。

sentences.en: So, and I really would like to not be yelling at, you know, my speaker in the morning while I'm having my coffee.
sentences.zh: 所以，我真的不想在早上喝咖啡的时候，对着我的音箱大喊大叫。

sentences.en: There's a prayer that I pray, and I call it the nuclear prayer.
sentences.zh: 我有一个祷告，我称之为“核弹祷告”。

sentences.en: And when you pray that prayer, it's a really strong prayer.
sentences.zh: 当你做那个祷告时，那是一个非常有力的祷告。

sentences.en: You don't pray it unless you're ready for the outcome.
sentences.zh: 除非你做好了面对结果的准备，否则不要轻易祷告。

sentences.en: And the nuclear prayer is very simple.
sentences.zh: 这个“核弹祷告”非常简单。

sentences.en: You pray to improve or to remove.
sentences.zh: 你祈求改善，或者祈求移除。

sentences.en: I prayed that prayer before the election.
sentences.zh: 我在大选前做过那个祷告。

sentences.en: I prayed it more than once before the election.
sentences.zh: 在大选前我不止一次地做过那个祷告。

sentences.en: I prayed that God improve, but I also prayed that he removed anyone and any person who did not have man's best interest at heart.
sentences.zh: 我祈求上帝改善，但我也祈求他移除任何没有把人类最大利益放在心上的人。

sentences.en: And there's an old spiritual that says he may not come when you want him, but he'll be there right on time.
sentences.zh: 有一首古老的灵歌说，他可能不会在你想要的时候出现，但他一定会准时到达。

sentences.en: He is God.
sentences.zh: 他是上帝。

sentences.en: And so with that being the case, it didn't happen immediately, but it was there right on time.
sentences.zh: 既然如此，虽然没有立即发生，但他确实准时到达了。

sentences.en: I think that America needs a breath of fresh air.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国需要一股新鲜空气。

sentences.en: Um, we are tired of being locked up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们厌倦了被封锁。

sentences.en: We are tired of being captive to a tyrant.
sentences.zh: 我们厌倦了成为暴君的俘虏。

sentences.en: We are tired of everything being about me, me, me, me, me, me, me, me, me, and not about us.
sentences.zh: 我们厌倦了所有事情都围绕着“我、我、我、我、我、我、我、我、我”，而不是围绕着“我们”。

sentences.en: Uh, U.S., when you put it together, is us.
sentences.zh: 呃，美国（U.S.），当你把它合在一起时，就是“我们”（us）。

sentences.en: Simple.
sentences.zh: 很简单。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Late Tuesday night, President Trump granted clemency to his former White House advisor,
sentences.zh: 周二深夜，特朗普总统给予他前白宫顾问特赦，

sentences.en: Steve Bannon, who has been charged with defrauding Trump supporters in a fundraising scheme involving the border wall with Mexico.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫·班农，他被指控在涉及美墨边境墙的筹款计划中欺诈特朗普的支持者。

sentences.en: Bannon himself lobbied Trump for the pardon, one of many to friends and allies that are expected in the hours before Trump leaves office.
sentences.zh: 班农本人曾游说特朗普寻求赦免，这是特朗普离任前几个小时内预计会给予朋友和盟友的众多赦免之一。

sentences.en: And.
sentences.zh: 而且。

sentences.en: The last time the Senate convened, we had just reclaimed the Capitol from violent criminals who tried to stop Congress from doing our duty.
sentences.zh: 参议院上次开会时，我们刚刚从试图阻止国会履行职责的暴力罪犯手中夺回了国会大厦。

sentences.en: On his final full day as Senate Majority Leader,
sentences.zh: 在他担任参议院多数党领袖的最后一个完整工作日，

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell held President Trump directly responsible for the attack on the Capitol during a speech from the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 米奇·麦康奈尔在参议院发言时，直接将国会大厦遇袭事件归咎于特朗普总统。

sentences.en: The mob was fed lies.
sentences.zh: 暴徒被灌输了谎言。

sentences.en: They were provoked by the president and other powerful people.
sentences.zh: 他们是被总统和其他有权势的人煽动的。

sentences.en: The remarks reinforce the view that McConnell is open to convicting Trump of inciting violence when the impeachment process moves from the House to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 这些言论强化了这样一种观点，即当弹劾程序从众议院移交到参议院时，麦康奈尔对判定特朗普煽动暴力罪持开放态度。

sentences.en: McConnell ended his speech by vowing a peaceful transfer of power later this morning.
sentences.zh: 麦康奈尔在演讲结束时发誓，今天上午晚些时候将实现权力的和平过渡。

sentences.en: We'll have a safe and successful inaugural right here on the West Front of the Capitol, the space that President Bush 41 called
sentences.zh: 我们将在国会大厦西侧广场举行一场安全且成功的就职典礼，这里曾被老布什总统称为

sentences.en: democracy's front porch.
sentences.zh: 民主的前廊。

sentences.en: The inauguration of President-elect Biden and Vice President-elect Harris is scheduled to begin at 1130 a.m.
sentences.zh: 当选总统拜登和当选副总统哈里斯的就职典礼定于东部时间上午11点30分开始。

sentences.en: Eastern.
sentences.zh: 东部时间。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Nina Patuk,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由尼娜·帕图克制作，

sentences.en: Alexander Lee Young, Sydney Harper, Austin Mitchell, Leslie Davis, Rochelle Bonja, Eric Krupke, and Jessica Chung.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·李·杨、悉尼·哈珀、奥斯汀·米切尔、莱斯利·戴维斯、罗谢尔·邦贾、埃里克·克鲁普克和杰西卡·钟。

sentences.en: It was edited by MJ Davis-Linn, Paige Coward, and Lisa Tobin, and engineered by Chris
sentences.zh: 由MJ·戴维斯-林、佩奇·考沃德和丽莎·托宾编辑，由克里斯负责工程制作

sentences.en: Wood.
sentences.zh: 伍德。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天

sentences.en: when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场痛苦、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me,
sentences.zh: 在我和我主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，

sentences.en: Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 莎拉·凯尼格，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你收听播客的地方都可以收听。
